extra.message: SQL Injection in login query — Authentication bypass and full read access to the users table (credential theft) via crafted username/password input [verified: Username/password from request.form are f-string interpolated directly into the SQL query at line 33 with no parameterization or sanitization.]

Missing authentication / forgeable session cookie on dashboard — Full account impersonation without credentials by simply setting a `session` cookie to any username [verified: dashboard route only checks presence of a 'session' cookie with no signature or server-side validation, so setting session=admin grants impersonation.]

Reflected XSS via session cookie on dashboard — Arbitrary JavaScript execution in the victim's browser (session theft, further attacks) [verified: Cookie value set from raw username at login and freely settable by client, reflected unescaped into HTML at line 47 with no output encoding.]

Plaintext password storage — Full credential exposure if the database file is read or leaked (e.g. via the SQLi above), enabling direct account takeover and credential reuse attacks [verified: Passwords stored and compared as plaintext strings in SQLite with no hashing.]

Insecure session cookie flags — Session cookie can be stolen via XSS (document.cookie) or network interception, enabling session hijacking [verified: set_cookie call at line 38 has no HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite flags and app runs over plain HTTP.]

Hardcoded default credentials — Attackers with source/db access obtain valid default credentials [verified: USERNAME/PASSWORD constants hardcoded in source, and default user1/password1 row seeded unconditionally on every startup.]
